points: Hitler Mussolini Simeon Flores, 45, won the mayoral race in Queropalca.
Flores will assume office on 1 January.
The victory was against a far-right candidate in the central Huánuco region.

summaries.summary: Burnham questioned over plans to expedite electoral changes, including scrapping photo ID for voting.
points: Plans include lowering voting age to 16 and tightening political donation rules.
Ministers reportedly want to halve the time for Lords to scrutinize the legislation.
Speculation exists that Burnham's advisers are pushing for an early general election.

summaries.summary: UK Defence Secretary supports Zelenskyy despite Trump calling for a new Ukrainian leader.
points: Wes Streeting asserts Ukrainians should choose their leader.
Trump's call coincides with US agreement to buy Russian diesel.
Priority is to maintain Western unity over Russia conflict.

summaries.summary: A developer paid people to test and provide feedback on their README documentation to improve its clarity and usability.
summaries.significance: This story matters because it highlights the importance of user testing for technical documentation, showing how real user feedback can significantly improve the clarity and usability of README files.
points: Paid €25 per person for an hour of feedback on the installation experience.
Updated the README after each session based on the difficulties users encountered.
Found that real human feedback was more valuable than using language models for simulation.

summaries.summary: The GNU Project advises developers to avoid GitHub due to its harmful practices and its role as a SaaSS (Service as a Software Substitute) dis-service.
points: GitHub's Copilot feature has been controversial for generating code that may infringe on copyright and for overwhelming project maintainers with low-quality bug reports.
GitHub's model ties users into a centralized system, limiting the use of free software Git by requiring interactions through nonfree JavaScript and spyware-laden tools.

summaries.summary: LineageOS released version 24.0, featuring security updates and UI improvements, ahead of its 10-year anniversary in 2026.
points: Security patches from August 2025 to October 2026 merged into LineageOS 18.1 through 24.0.
LineageOS 24.0 includes UI/UX refinements and Material Design 3 updates for core apps.
New browser-based flash tools using WebUSB introduced for easier device installation.

summaries.summary: The size of a Git commit varies based on file compressibility and directory structure.
points: Committing 3 bytes of change in a directory of 50 files results in kilobytes of overhead.
Larger commits with fewer files can store data as little as 10% of the uncompressed size.
A single tiny file commit shows substantial overhead, indicating larger commits save space.

summaries.summary: Nitter seeks funding and legal help after receiving cease and desist letters from X Corp.
points: X Corp sent cease and desist letters on 24 August 2026 and 8 September 2026.
Previous assurances about legal representation were found to be untrue.
Donations will prioritize legal costs, with surplus supporting Nitter or its successor.

summaries.summary: IRCv3 specifications detail modern IRC protocol enhancements and extensions.
points: Standardised account login using SASL for quicker registration.
Instant away notifications for real-time user status updates.
Support for Unicode nicknames and channel names for international users.

summaries.summary: Cloudflare acquires Deno, aiming to support celld development while ceasing Deno runtime development after a year.
summaries.significance: The acquisition shifts focus from Deno to celld, impacting the future development and maintenance of Deno's runtime.
points: Cloudflare will support Deno runtime with monthly updates for one year post-acquisition.
Deno's creator, Ryan Dahl, sees celld as more aligned with building new abstractions.
Deno introduced a permissions system for specifying file and network access, now partially mirrored in Node.js.

summaries.summary: UN warns that developing nations are at risk of a triple shock from energy crisis, El Niño, and high borrowing costs, potentially pushing millions back into poverty.
summaries.significance: The story highlights the urgent need for international support to prevent tens of millions in developing nations from falling back into poverty due to compounded crises.
points: UNDP’s administrator Alexander De Croo calls for urgent international support.
Crises could push tens or hundreds of millions back into poverty.
Warning comes ahead of IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok.

summaries.summary: Developers often assume consistency can be achieved within a single component, but Apache Kafka's journey illustrates the complexity.
points: Achieving exactly-once writes in Kafka took years and multiple new components.
Exactly-once processing requires an end-to-end guarantee, not just within components.
Eight years after initial release, Kafka's protocol was still being redesigned for correctness.
